 1          Pursuant to Civil Local Rules 6-1(b), 6-2, and 7-12, Plaintiffs Marissa Porcuna, Karen
 2   Schreiman, Romy Edge, and Celestina Benn (“Plaintiffs”) and Defendant The Talbots LLC
 3   (“Defendant,” and together with Plaintiffs, the “Parties”), by and through their respective counsel,
 4   hereby stipulate and respectfully request that the Court continue the hearing on Defendant’s Motion
 5   to Dismiss Plaintiffs’ First Amended Complaint and the Case Management Conference, both
 6   scheduled to be heard in person before the Honorable Judge Haywood S. Gilliam, Jr., at 2:00 p.m., in
 7

15
     and Defendant filed its Reply on June 3, 2026 (Dkt. 34);
16

17

18

19
     practice law for fewer than five years, to argue the Motion on Defendant’s behalf;
20
            WHEREAS, Christine Wang recently joined Ballard Spahr and Defendant’s litigation team
21
22   and is available to argue the Motion on October 15, 2026, or another date thereafter;

23          WHEREAS, Section 10 of the Court’s Standing Order for Civil Cases reflects the Court’s

24   support for providing attorneys who have been licensed for five or fewer years with opportunities to

25   present oral argument;

26          WHEREAS, if the Court is not inclined to continue the hearing, the Parties alternatively

27   request permission to appear remotely for the Case Management Conference and to argue the Motion

28   on September 24, 2026;

 1          WHEREAS, Section 17 of the Court’s Standing Order provides that an attorney may appear
 2   remotely at a motion hearing upon a showing of good cause and requires any request to appear
 3   remotely to be filed at least one week before the hearing and an in-person appearance;
 4          WHEREAS, the Parties are filing this request on September 16, 2026, at least one week
 5   before the September 24, 2026 hearing and good cause exists to allow the Parties to appear remotely
 6   because Plaintiff’s counsel is located in Southern California and Portland, Oregon, and would require
 7
     substantial travel time and expense for a hearing at which the briefing is complete and no evidence
 8
     will be presented; and
 9
            WHEREAS, the requested continuance will not alter the completed briefing on Defendant’s
10
     Motion or affect any other existing deadlines in this action, this is the Parties first request to continue
11
     the hearing on Defendant’s Motion and the Case Management Conference, the requested continuance
12
     is not sought for purposes of delay, and neither party will be prejudiced by the requested relief.
13
            NOW, THEREFORE, the Parties respectfully stipulate and request that the Court:
14
        1. Continue the hearing on Defendant’s Motion and the Case Management Conference from
15
            September 24, 2026 to October 15, 2026, or another date convenient for the Court; or
16
        2. Alternatively, retain the September 24, 2026 hearing date and permit the Parties to appear
17
            remotely and argue Defendant’s Motion and attend the Case Management Conference.
18
